desire_meter.name: Desire Meter
desire_meter.idea: Plan your wants. Bottled-up wants explode — a planned treat costs less than an impulse splurge.
desire_meter.how1: The meter rises every year, and every time you Save or Invest (resisting).
desire_meter.how2: Spend when the meter is 50+ = a planned treat: meter back to 0, no lifestyle creep.
desire_meter.how3: If the meter reaches 100, next year you splurge on impulse: 15% of your net worth gone.

saving_streak.name: Saving Streak
saving_streak.idea: Pay yourself first. Small amounts every single year beat big amounts once in a while.
saving_streak.how1: Every year you Save or Invest, your streak grows by 1.
saving_streak.how2: Each new year an Auto-SIP goes into your index fund — bigger with a longer streak (max at 5).
saving_streak.how3: One Spend breaks the streak and the Auto-SIP stops until you rebuild it.

lifestyle_creep.name: Lifestyle Creep & Slots
lifestyle_creep.idea: When your income rises, don't let your lifestyle rise with it — invest the raise in a few good assets.
lifestyle_creep.how1: You get a salary every year with a 10% raise — but lifestyle quietly takes 5% more of it each year.
lifestyle_creep.how2: Spend: lifestyle +12%. Save = budget review: lifestyle −10%.
lifestyle_creep.how3: Only 3 investment slots (different assets). Choose quality: index funds, equity, debt.

grihastha.name: Family Goals & Insurance
grihastha.idea: Money for known goals should be ready in safe places, and insurance should carry big health shocks.
grihastha.how1: Year 4: home down payment. Year 7: kids' education. Pay from cash, FD or debt fund.
grihastha.how2: Not enough ready money? Investments are sold in a hurry and you pay 20% extra on the shortfall.
grihastha.how3: Boss, year 9: parents in hospital (20% of net worth). Health insurance equipped = you pay only a fifth.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: BHAO is a competitive, multiplayer financial card game designed to simulate the real Indian economy. Players navigate real-world financial situations like SIP investments, IPO booms, and unexpected market crashes. The objective is to be the first player to accumulate ₹50 Lakhs in wealth while defending against attacks from other players.
faq.q2: How does the stock simulator work?
faq.a2: Unlike traditional stock simulators, BHAO uses a dynamic event-driven system. Players draw "Decision Cards" where they must choose between safe saving or risky investing. Successful investments yield high returns, but carry the risk of total loss. Special "Action Cards" allow players to trigger market-wide events that affect the entire economy.
faq.q3: Can I play BHAO for free?
faq.a3: Yes, BHAO is completely free to play. You can create an account, build your wealth, climb the Mogul Rank Ladder, and compete with friends in multiplayer rooms without any cost. The game focuses on improving financial literacy through strategic gameplay.

invest.title: Invest early, let years do the work
invest.body: Idle cash loses ~6% a year to inflation. An index fund grows with the market — bumpy years, strong decades.

emergency.title: Keep an emergency fund
emergency.body: Cash for surprises means you never sell investments in a hurry — Rahul paid a 15% penalty selling his flat.

insure.title: Insure the big risks
insure.body: Health insurance turned a hospital bill into ₹0. In BHAO, equipping a defense is free and doesn’t end your turn.

scam.title: “Guaranteed returns” = red flag
scam.body: Hot tips and double-your-money schemes vanish. Check SEBI/RBI registration before you invest.

networth.title: Your money
networth.body: Net worth = cash + investments. You start with {{cash}} in cash and no investments. Each round of BHAO is one year of your life. Grow your net worth toward {{goal}}.

rival.title: Meet {{name}}
rival.body: Rahul has the same {{netWorth}} net worth, but {{flat}} of it is a flat and only {{cash}} is cash. He invests every spare rupee and keeps no emergency fund. Keep an eye on him.

pickChai.title: Play a card
pickChai.body: Each turn you play one card. This one is about the ₹150 a day you spend on chai and snacks — ₹4,500 a month.

preview.title: Save, Spend or Invest?
preview.body: Each choice shows what it does to your money right now. Save adds cash. Spend costs cash and makes your lifestyle more expensive. Invest moves cash into an investment — your net worth stays the same today, then grows (or dips) every year.

invest.title: Invest it
invest.body: An index fund owns a slice of India's top companies. Invest moves {{amount}} of your cash into it — no instant profit, it grows year by year.
invest.bodyPart: An index fund owns a slice of India's top companies. Invest moves part of your cash into it — no instant profit, it grows year by year.

botTurn.title: Rahul’s turn
botTurn.body: You play one card, then your turn ends. Now Rahul plays — he puts his cash into more property.

year.title: A year passed
year.market: The market moved: your index fund went {{pct}}, {{from}} → {{to}}.
year.inflation: Inflation ({{pct}}% a year) ate {{amount}} of your idle cash: prices went up, so the same rupees buy less. Cash that just sits there quietly shrinks.
year.inflationSome: Inflation ({{pct}}% a year) ate some of your idle cash: prices went up, so the same rupees buy less. Cash that just sits there quietly shrinks.

lure.title: Life event: a “hot tip”
lure.body: Each year can bring a life event. Rahul got a WhatsApp tip — “guaranteed 30% a month!” — and put {{amount}} into it. Let’s see how that goes.
lure.bodyNoAmount: Each year can bring a life event. Rahul got a WhatsApp tip — “guaranteed 30% a month!” — and put money into it. Let’s see how that goes.

pickSave.title: Keep a buffer
pickSave.body: You have {{cash}} in cash. Investing all of it is risky: life throws surprise bills. Keep some cash as an emergency fund.

botTurn2.title: Saved!
botTurn2.body: Your cash is now {{cash}}. Rahul is playing — he invests again and keeps almost no cash.

medical.title: Medical emergency!
medical.head: Rahul slipped and needed hospital care.
medical.headBill: Rahul slipped and needed hospital care — his net worth fell by {{amount}}.
medical.sold: He had too little cash, so he was forced to sell part of his flat in a hurry at a 15% penalty.
medical.you: You keep {{cash}} in cash, so a bill like that would be paid from cash and your investments keep growing. That is what an emergency fund is for.

equip.title: Get insured
equip.body: You drew Health Insurance. Defense cards block a kind of trouble — this one blocks medical bills. Equipping a defense is free: it does not use up your turn.
equip.todo: Tap the glowing “{{card}}” card, then 🛡️ Equip.

freePlay.title: Still your turn
freePlay.body: Insurance is on. You can still play one card this turn — your call. Invest, save or spend: you know what each does now.

botTurn3.body: Rahul plays. Then another year passes…

scam.title: Where did the hot tip go?
scam.wiped: Rahul’s “guaranteed” tip crashed two years in a row and is now wiped out. Guaranteed high returns are how scams work.
scam.crashing: Rahul’s “guaranteed” tip keeps crashing. Guaranteed high returns are how scams work.
scam.blocked: And a hospital bill hit you this year — your Health Insurance blocked it, so you paid nothing.

goal.title: The goal
goal.p1: Grow your net worth to the goal before your rivals — or be the richest when the years run out.
goal.p2: One round = one year of your life. Everyone plays one turn per year.

cash.title: Cash vs investments
cash.p2: You hold {{hand}} cards. Each turn play one card: Save (adds cash), Spend (costs cash, raises your lifestyle) or Invest (moves cash into an index fund, gold, property…).
cash.p3: Equipping a defense is free (up to {{maxDefenses}}). Or Pass: discard one card and end your turn.

year.title: A year passes
year.p1: Every investment moves with the market: steady ones a little, risky ones a lot — crashes happen.
year.p2: Inflation eats about {{inflation}}% of idle cash each year (more if you keep spending on lifestyle).
year.p3: So invest what you won’t need — but keep some cash.

events.title: Life events & defenses
events.p1: Most years bring a life event: a bonus, a hospital bill, a job gap, a “guaranteed” scam tip…
events.p2: Bills are paid from cash. No cash? Your investments get sold in a hurry, at a penalty. That’s why you keep an emergency fund.
events.p3: Defense cards like Health Insurance block whole kinds of trouble.
